docs.title: How to use test cards
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards
docs.snippet: When you work with a test card, use test API keys in all API calls. This is true whether you’re serving a payment form to test interactively or writing test code.

docs.title: Testing interactively
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards > Testing interactively
docs.snippet: When testing interactively, use a card number, such as 4242 4242 4242 4242. Enter the card number in the Dashboard or in any payment form.

docs.title: Test code
docs.heading_path: Testing > How to use test cards > Test code
docs.snippet: When writing test code, use a PaymentMethod such as pm_card_visa instead of a card number. We don’t recommend using card numbers directly in API calls or server-side code, even in testing environments. If you use them, your code might not be PCI-compliant when you go live. By…

docs.title: Fraud prevention
docs.heading_path: Testing > Fraud prevention
docs.snippet: Stripe’s fraud prevention system, Radar, can block payments when they have a high risk level or fail verification checks. You can use the cards in this section to test your Radar settings. You can also use them to test how your integration responds to blocked payments.

docs.title: Review expected webhook sequence by payment method
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review expected webhook sequence by payment method
docs.snippet: The test values for each method are in the Test a non-card payment method section. Use the following tables to understand which webhook sequence to expect when you use those test values.

docs.title: Review bank debit webhook sequence
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review bank debit webhook sequence
docs.snippet: All bank debit methods follow the processing to succeeded or payment_failed pattern. In test mode, transitions happen after about 3 minutes for account numbers that simulate a delay. These use a 9 prefix or suffix. See the test values for each method in the referenced section.

docs.title: Review voucher-based webhook sequence
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review voucher-based webhook sequence
docs.snippet: Voucher methods issue a payment code that your customer pays out of band. The PaymentIntent enters requires_action immediately after confirmation. The delayed outcome arrives when your customer pays or when the voucher expires.

docs.title: Review redirect and delayed notification method
docs.heading_path: Testing > Test asynchronous payment methods > Review redirect and delayed notification method
docs.snippet: Some payment methods redirect your customer for authentication. Depending on the payment method and configuration, Stripe might confirm the final outcome immediately after the redirect or deliver it asynchronously.
